comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026–2027 Mechanical Engineering after-revision PER Articles 3.3–3.5 and programme appendices were freshly retrieved and inspected on 8 October 2026. Article 3.3 establishes English instruction, correcting normalized NLD-only metadata while preserving raw NLD provenance. The ordinary degree is core 125 including 4WC00 Bachelor Final Project 10, ITEC 10 and genuine free space 45. The 28 positions total 180: year one core 55 + ITEC 5; year two core 40 + electives 20; year three core 30 including project + ITEC 5 + electives 25. Two restricted third-year core options are instantiated as the first alternatives in the displayed Q3 and Q4 groups:4CC50 Design Principles for Precision ME and 4CBLC30 Mechanical Design Project, each 5. Selection is independent of UCR fit; no named graduation route is invented and all eight alternatives are not universally compulsory. Optional summer 4WC30 Precision in High-tech Systems is distinct from selected 4CC50 and is not added. PPD is embedded in existing credits; seven MyFuture points, five Studium Generale activities for ITEC and mandatory CANS(RSI), HSE and ICT training do not add EC. Free 45 requires at least 30 at levels 2/3 including 15 at level 3, approval and non-overlap. BEP entry requires at least 120 credits and all compulsory first-year components. It may be taken in any quarter, over two quarters with other work or as a single-quarter block; exact future scheduling and admission remain conditions. No new UCR judgment is made.

Programming, algorithms, machine perception, robotics and automated systems
Product development, prototyping and engineering-design decisions

alternatives.label: Mechanical-system modelling, robotics & intelligent control
alternatives.concept: Combine mathematical and numerical system models with programming, algorithms, image-based perception, robotics, machine learning, networks and product design to study automated mechanical systems. This is a computational systems response, not Mechanical Engineering equivalence.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule contains a cumulative mathematical/computational sequence, linear systems, numerical methods, computer vision, robotics, networks and product design; the label avoids claiming mechanics, thermofluids, materials or manufacturing engineering.
progression: All exact Fall 2026-start availability and recorded formal prerequisites pass. Programming precedes algorithms, networks, planning and reinforcement learning; Mathematical Methods precedes dependent mathematics, robotics and neural networks. Numerical Methods and Linear Systems occur in the sole available fourth semester, while Advanced Calculus follows when next offered.

alternatives.label: Sustainable energy, product systems & intelligent automation
alternatives.concept: Retain mathematical modelling, perception, robotics and intelligent decisions while adding lifecycle assessment, renewable-energy design, climate context and material recovery for lower-impact products and industrial systems.
alternatives.labelReason: Five sustainability courses create a cumulative lifecycle, energy and resource strand alongside quantitative intelligent-system methods; the label does not imply thermodynamics, manufacturing, propulsion or mechanical design.
progression: All exact Fall 2026-start availability and recorded formal prerequisites pass. Sustainability Essentials I precedes II, which precedes Renewable System Design and resource recovery. Programming and Mathematical Methods precede their dependent advanced courses. Advanced Calculus follows Numerical Methods and Linear Systems because its next exact offering is the final spring.
alternatives.distinctness: Five courses / 37.5 EC differ in each direction. Logic, databases, networks, advanced algorithms and AI ethics are replaced by two sustainability foundations, climate change, renewable-system design and resource recovery; these are concept-driven changes.

candidates.label: Sustainable energy and efficient product systems
Mechanics, thermofluids, materials and precision manufacturing

selection.assessment: Two related-fields responses pass the academic, schedule and 30-EC distinctness gates. The first owns the modelling, robotics, automation and product-design interests through actual mathematical and computational content. The second is independently supported by sustainable-energy, efficient-manufacturing and lifecycle interests. A mechanics, thermofluids, materials and precision-manufacturing direction cannot supply statics and dynamics, solid mechanics, thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics, mechanical vibration, finite elements, metrology, machining or mechanical laboratories. General calculus, linear systems, robotics and renewable-system assessment cannot be relabelled as that physical-engineering formation. No third programme is manufactured.

blocks: Both establish calculus used in quantitative engineering models; UCR also includes matrices and differential equations but is not mechanical-engineering mathematics.
Both use numerical methods to solve engineering-relevant equations; the external course applies them specifically to fluids and solids, which UCR does not reproduce.
Both develop probability and statistical reasoning for quantitative engineering analysis.
Both study signals and linear-system representations; UCR supplies the mathematical system framework without the surrounding mechanical laboratories.
Both include programming and computational problem solving; the external component also teaches mechanical design principles that UCR programming does not reproduce.
Both engage robotic systems; UCR teaches computational kinematics, planning and manipulation, while the external challenge integrates mechanical construction and engineering practice.
Both involve product-development and design decisions with prototypes and quantitative analysis; UCR concerns consumer products rather than precision mechanical engineering.
Both address sustainable energy choices; UCR evaluates renewable-system designs, while the external challenge develops mechanical-engineering decisions around sustainable fuels.

notes.text: The UCR alternatives support mathematical system modelling, programming, robotics, intelligent control, product development and sustainable-energy analysis. They do not reproduce the target’s mechanics, dynamics, thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics, solid mechanics, materials science, manufacturing, precision engineering, mechanical laboratories or Mechanical Engineering capstone.
